eastern-reaches.name: Eastern Reaches
eastern-reaches.description: A hardworking region with strong community ties, known for producing grassroots talent.

clubs.name: Honeybell AFC
clubs.club_history: Founded by orchard farmers and beekeepers in 1935, Honeybell AFC is a community-focused club known for nurturing young talent. Their kits and badge feature blooming orchards and buzzing bees.
club_values: Buzzing energy, grassroot passion, youth first
clubs.club_slogan: From the Orchard, To the Pitch

clubs.name: Blackpick FC
clubs.club_history: Founded by miners, Blackpick FC grew from the local union’s league. Gritty, old-school football is their brand, with a loyal fanbase that thrives on underdog energy.

clubs.name: Union of the Forge
clubs.club_history: Formed by foundry workers and engineers, Union of the Forge emphasizes work ethic, unity, and calculated football. Matches often resemble chess with boots.

clubs.name: Molten Boots FC
clubs.club_history: Named after the slag paths of smelters where they trained, Molten Boots FC is known for fast, aggressive play and fiery atmosphere at home matches.

clubs.name: Braknov Royals
clubs.club_history: Originally established as a school sports program for military officer families, Braknov Royals evolved into a semi-professional club under royal subsidy. Their tactical style is calm and composed, modeled after elite British academy football. They represent the refined face of a hardened border town.

clubs.name: Braknov Spartak
clubs.club_history:
Braknov Spartak was founded shortly after the Great Eastern Uprising as a military sports club, originally designed to improve fitness among border patrol officers. That legacy still lives on in their identity: rigid defensive shapes, intense work rate, and zero tolerance for theatrics.
The club is funded by the Velmoran Armed Sports Foundation, giving it stability but limiting risky ventures. Its academy produces tactically aware defenders and hard-working midfielders who are often recruited by bigger clubs.
Their stadium, The Bastion, is a brutalist fortress — tall, imposing, with banners of military mottos and historical war heroes adorning the walls. No nonsense. No excuses. No flair — that's the Spartak way.
The “Iron Curtain Derby” vs Valdren Atletika is rooted in history: post-war tensions, political polarization, and clashing ideologies. It's the most intense and ideologically charged fixture in the country.
Though they haven't lifted a top-tier title, Spartak are the spine of Velmoran footballing culture — a club feared, never pitied.
clubs.club_slogan: “Steel Walls Stand, Never Fall – Spartak Answers Duty’s Call!”

clubs.name: Sootmark Town
clubs.club_history: Founded by street footballers and workers in the smokehouse district of Lurngrad, the club is rebellious and unpolished, known for a fierce, scrappy style.

clubs.name: Blossomridge FC
clubs.club_history: Started by schoolteachers and botanists, Blossomridge FC is beloved for elegant passing football, floral-themed kits, and a locally famous youth academy.

clubs.name: Daisybank Wanderers
clubs.club_history: Daisybank Wanderers were established by textile workers and seamstresses in the daisy fields near Lurngrad. The club has a poetic, romantic style — often underdogs but widely loved for their charm and loyal away fans.

clubs.name: Bluehollow Atlantic
clubs.club_history: Born from a coastal shipping firm’s youth initiative, Bluehollow Atlantic grew from beachside leagues into a semi-professional force. Now fully professional, they’re known for swift counter-attacking play and wide formations — a mirror to the rhythm of the sea. Their sponsorship with oceanic NGOs gives the club a unique eco-mission among peers.
clubs.club_slogan: Ride the wave, rule the pitch.

clubs.name: Lurngrad United
clubs.club_history:
Lurngrad United is a post-war club, created as a unity project to bind fragmented districts of Lurngrad into a single civic force. With its founding rooted in collaboration, it has long been a model of local engagement and democratic gover[]ce.
Owned by the Lurngrad Trade Alliance — a coalition of local businesses and civic groups — the club is stable, community-accountable, and strategically smart. It walks the line between ambition and responsibility.
Lurngrad United has quickly gained attention for developing Velmora’s next generation of technical midfielders, thanks to their academy partnerships with local colleges and the national institute of sport.
The stadium, Griffin’s Nest, is known for its vibrant mixed fan zones, youth showcases, and election-style supporter forums where fans vote on aesthetic elements (kits, anthems, mascots).
Though Lurngrad United has no silverware yet, they’re regarded as Velmora’s model club for growth — both fi[]cially and ethically.
club_values: “Built by the city, for the future.”
clubs.club_slogan: “One City, One Fight – Griffins Soar Through Day and Night!”

clubs.name: Plumstead Juniors
clubs.club_history: Plumstead Juniors started as a school club and slowly rose to semi-professional ranks. They’re known for their commitment to giving local teenagers a route to senior football. Many players have used the club as a stepping stone to bigger academies.

clubs.name: Pebbleline Albion
clubs.club_history: Formed by lighthouse keepers and port workers, Pebbleline Albion is defined by wind, water, and long walks. A calm but serious club that plays structured football and values slow, steady growth over flash.

clubs.name: Bumblefield FC
clubs.club_history: Bumblefield FC was started by former Honeybell players who moved west in search of work. They kept the bee theme but added edge — more speed, less sweetness. Today, the club plays with pace and directness, known for quick transitions and sharp counters.

clubs.name: Ostravaj Sporting
clubs.club_history: Ostravaj Sporting was the civilian counterpart to the noble-founded Korona. While Korona catered to aristocracy, Sporting was founded by the town's artisans, athletes, and local guilds. Today, the club plays modern, expansive football with an eye on reclaiming regional glory. Their matches against Korona are dubbed the Duel of Crowns, with deep cultural undercurrents.

clubs.name: Ostravaj Korona
clubs.club_history:
Ostravaj Korona is Velmora’s royal oldest son — the first club to be officially endorsed by a noble estate. Formed by House Korona’s eastern landowners and tutors, the club has long positioned itself as football’s noble custodians, focusing on technical precision, sportsmanship, and defensive discipline.
The club is still partially funded by House Korona Holdings, an aristocratic endowment. Its influence is seen in the matchday attire, stadium architecture, and the club motto: “By Honor, With Precision.”
Home matches are played at Korona Crown Arena, a grand but quiet stadium near forested hills, featuring stone archways and royal banners. The venue is steeped in class, and matchdays feel ceremonial.
Though no longer a domi[]t force, Ostravaj Korona remains an essential figure in Velmora’s footballing tapestry — the thinking man’s club, where football is a chessboard of legacy.
clubs.club_slogan: “Wolves of Crown, Strike with Class – Ostravaj Stands First and Last!”

northern-highlands.name: Northern Highlands
northern-highlands.description: A rugged and traditional northern region known for its industrial towns and fierce derbies.

clubs.name: Cobbleglen United
clubs.club_history: Hailing from the icy forest hamlets near Sevrin, Cobbleglen United was founded by a group of quarrymen and foresters. Known for their old-school approach and dogged defending, the club prides itself on weathering both storms and opposition attacks.

clubs.name: Ashberry Juniors
clubs.club_history: A latecomer by Regional standards, Ashberry Juniors was established by a school network in Sevrin to promote education and youth development. Today, it’s a vibrant academy-driven club that values flair, speed, and future potential.

clubs.name: Little Nest AFC
clubs.club_history: Little Nest AFC, affectionately called “The Hatchlings,” started as a post-school youth program for orphans and displaced families. Their play style is cautious, calculated, and often aerial. They are deeply loved for their emotional origin story.

clubs.name: Sevrin North End
clubs.club_history: Formed during wartime by northern townships left out of Lokomotiv’s sphere, North End grew from frigid football fields and harsh wind. Known for long throws, snow games, and relentless pressing, they’re Sevrin’s blue-collar alternative.

clubs.name: Sevrin Lokomotiv
clubs.club_history:
Sevrin Lokomotiv is one of Velmora’s most historic football institutions, known for its strong ties to the railway industry and state infrastructure. Founded by transport workers, it became a symbol of national modernization during the mid-20th century.
In its heyday, Lokomotiv dominated the league thanks to state backing and a ruthlessly organized style of play. Though that political era ended, the club still embodies that identity: rigid systems, cold weather, steely mentality.
The club’s stadium, Lokomotiv Railstadion, sits at high altitude and often gets snow in spring matches — it's a dreaded away trip for southern clubs.
Today, Lokomotiv remains fi[]cially stable, if unspectacular. They don’t chase headlines, but they consistently develop youth, grind out results, and finish strong.
clubs.club_slogan: “Cold Winds Blow, Rails Run True – Lokomotiv Pulls Right Through!”

clubs.name: Cragshield United
clubs.club_history: Created by militia descendants in the foothills of Braskov, Cragshield United has always emphasized strength and self-defense, both tactically and culturally. They are known for deep blocks, bruising football, and loud home support in a steep stadium.

clubs.name: Shiverbell Athletic
clubs.club_history: Founded near an alpine monastery, Shiverbell is known for its poetic identity and a unique tradition: players ring a bronze bell pre-match. Their style is crisp and fluid in midfield, often drawing on finesse more than force.

clubs.name: Whitelantern FC
clubs.club_history: Whitelantern FC has roots in a Braskov university library. Known for their philosophical approach, their motto is engraved above the tunnel: “From Knowledge, Strength.” Tactically elegant, but lacking physicality in recent seasons.

clubs.name: Rudar Braskov
clubs.club_history: The second club of Braskov, Rudar was founded by coal miners seeking their own footballing identity, independent from Braskov Ruda. They're known for direct play, aerial domi[]ce, and trench-like mentality. Matches against Braskov Ruda are brutal and fiery — the Miners’ Rift.

clubs.name: Braskov Ruda
clubs.club_history:
Braskov Ruda emerged in the rugged mining settlements of western Velmora. The name "Ruda" means "ore" in Velmoran, and everything about the club—from its crimson kits to its dugouts—feels carved from the earth.
Originally formed by copper and coal workers, the club became a symbol of resistance during economic downturns and regime shifts. Locals see Ruda not just as a team, but as a shield against central neglect.
The club’s ownership reflects this: the Braskov Industrial Trust, a rem[]t of a state-owned mining enterprise, still funds the team with leftover endowments and civic pride.
The home ground, The Quarry, is a tight, sloped stadium surrounded by cold wind and shouting from metal bleachers. It’s a nightmare for technical sides.
The "Miner’s War" vs Karnov Ironfields is the blood-and-mud derby of Velmora — fewer passes, more bruises.
clubs.club_slogan: “We Bleed the Earth, We Stand for All – Braskov Rises, Never Falls!”

clubs.name: Northern Keepers
clubs.club_history: Originally formed as a goalkeeper training club, Northern Keepers evolved into a full squad of specialists in defensive transitions. Known for record clean sheets and gritty football, they view every goal conceded as a betrayal of identity.

clubs.name: Cobbleglen Rovers
clubs.club_history: A sibling club to United but with a rowdier, working-class origin, Cobbleglen Rovers emerged from coal trails and railyards. Feisty and community-centered, they pride themselves on big tackles, muddy wins, and ferocious local derbies.

clubs.name: Kresna Dynamo
clubs.club_history:
Kresna Dynamo began as a post-war workers’ club, originally associated with power stations and highland rail lines. But over time, its identity morphed from grit to glory.
With the 2010 takeover by Jozef Marek, a local tech-energy tycoon, the club saw an explosion of infrastructure, scouts, and investment. Marek built the Velmoran Football Intelligence Lab, which turned Kresna into a youth development juggernaut.
Now, they combine local wonderkids, South European flair, and cutting-edge analytics — a hybrid footballing machine of cold calculation and youthful chaos.
Their stadium, The Dynamo Spire, is ultra-modern and built for noise: sharp echoes, wide sightlines, snow-resistant heating coils. It's a fortress in winter.
Kresna’s mission? Become Velmora’s Ajax and its PSG in one. It’s not just about trophies — it’s about changing football.
clubs.club_slogan: “Ice in the Veins, Fire in the Feet – Kresna Fly, Never Defeat!”

clubs.name: Applebrook FC
clubs.club_history: Formed by orchard workers and cider cooperatives, Applebrook FC has a cult following and a reputation for producing tenacious young midfielders. Their play is earthy but energetic — a grassroots team with heart.

clubs.name: Thimbleby Town
clubs.club_history: One of the smallest clubs in the league, Thimbleby is a village outfit that plays with giant-slaying spirit. Crowds are tiny but noisy, the pitch is tight, and their tactical blueprint is built around hard pressing and counterattacks.

clubs.name: Novastral Unity
clubs.club_history: Novastral Unity was formed by alumni and students of Novastral Tech University aiming to create a democratic, grassroots football model. The club is entirely fan-owned, digitally governed, and driven by the values of collective action, inclusivity, and tactical evolution.
clubs.club_slogan: Together we rise, digitally we play.

clubs.name: Novastral Zenith
clubs.club_history:
Novastral Zenith was created as a university sports project in partnership with local science institutes and tech entrepreneurs. It evolved into a professional club in the early 2000s, and rose steadily thanks to a rigorous data-driven approach to tactics, fitness, and recruitment.
Owned by Toma Zaric, a software visionary and founder of ZenithAI, the club represents the future of Velmoran football — progressive, optimized, and dynamic.
Nicknamed "The Astrals", Zenith has invested heavily in its academy, attracting the brightest youth talent in the country. They pioneered GPS tracking, neurocognitive training, and AI-assisted opposition scouting in Velmora.
Their stadium, Astro Heights Park, also called, The Observatory, features AR match stats in-stadium, solar panels, and zero-waste food zones — a model for sustainability and innovation.
Though traditionalists mock them as a “spreadsheet club,” their results are silencing critics, and their future looks stellar.
clubs.club_slogan: “Eyes on Stars, Feet on Fire – Novastral Will Always Climb Higher!”

southern-lakes.name: Southern Lakes
southern-lakes.description: Picturesque towns and lakefront stadiums define this region, with clubs rich in local identity.

clubs.name: Red Quarry Rovers
clubs.club_history: Founded by quarrymen in the red-stone canyons east of Drosna, Red Quarry Rovers reflect the region’s grit and solidarity. The club rose to prominence in the post-war era, briefly reaching the second tier, and still carries a rugged underdog spirit.

clubs.name: Rustfield Rovers
clubs.club_history: Built in a rustbelt village near the southern train line, Rustfield are known for their defensive resilience and tough, hard-to-break identity. They are famous for their iron-gray kits and their “Forge Block” defensive shape.

clubs.name: FK Drosna Lok
clubs.club_history: Created as the industrial works team for Drosna’s growing logistics and ferry industries, Drosna Lok is the younger sibling of Drosna FK. Known for a more pragmatic, fast-break style, they take pride in being a people’s alternative to the more polished Drosna FK.
clubs.club_slogan: We move. We break. We conquer.

clubs.name: Drosna FK
clubs.club_history:
Drosna FK is Velmora’s thinking club — long praised for its measured football, deep-rooted philosophy, and historical elegance. Founded by lakeside merchants and teachers, the club fostered education, strategy, and sportsmanship as core values from the start.
Municipally owned, it is supported by the City of Drosna, which ensures it is not just a team but a symbol of the city’s identity. The team colors and crest reflect the Lake Dros, calm but deep — just like their style.
Famous for a 4-3-3 possession system, Drosna’s midfield play is admired even abroad. Its academy regularly sends players to the national team and abroad — most notably in midfield and full-back roles.
The stadium, The Mirror Shore, sits beside the lake — calm in scenery, intense in atmosphere. Supporters sing "The Stillness Before the Storm", a hymn known for echoing across the water.
Drosna FK is known not just for winning — but for winning well. A gentle giant with a scalpel, not a sledgehammer.
clubs.club_slogan: “Calm as the Lake, Sharp as the Blade – Drosna Will Not Fade!”

clubs.name: Hearthside United
clubs.club_history: Hearthside was established in the southern quarter of Radomir by local merchants and teachers seeking unity through football. The club’s legacy centers on family warmth, local loyalty, and slow-burning rise through consistency.

clubs.name: Golden Acre FC
clubs.club_history: Golden Acre FC represents the farmland towns of southern Radomir. The club is rooted in agricultural cooperatives, and players often emerge from local schools. Known for field discipline and set-piece strength.

clubs.name: Crowspire FC
clubs.club_history: Dark horses of the south, founded by scholars and hunters. Specialize in unpredictable counter-attacks.

clubs.name: Radomir Veles
clubs.club_history: Radomir Veles was built around the athletic academy of the Radomir Noble Academy, focusing on speed, elevation, and raw flair. A more expressive and bohemian alternative to the conservative Radomir Eagles, Veles is about instinctive talent and spirited play.

clubs.name: Radomir Eagles
clubs.club_history:
Radomir Eagles were established under royal patronage by the House of Radomir, and still receive ceremonial support from the Velmoran Crown Estate. Originally a team of officers, nobles, and philosophers, the club has evolved into Velmora’s high-society representative in the game.
Their stadium, The Red Talon Stadium, is a domed, red-accented architectural marvel. Known for velvet seating, curated club music, and a strict “white tie” dress code in the heritage stand.
Owned partially by the Crown Estate, the club is governed by a conservative board and guided by deep cultural legacy. It operates on measured budgets, avoids controversy, and values decorum, tactical control, and long-term reputation above short-term gain.
Despite not dominating the league in recent decades, Radomir remains the most respected club in Velmora’s elite circles, and a key part of the league’s history and identity.
clubs.club_slogan: “By Crown, By Right – Radomir Soars into the Night!”

clubs.name: Ploughline Albion
clubs.club_history: Founded by farming syndicates along the Vernek plains, Ploughline Albion’s traditions are tied to the land and rhythm of seasons. Always tactically compact, and often upset bigger teams with organized pressing and long throws.

clubs.name: Meadowbell Athletic
clubs.club_history: Founded in the meadows outside Vernek by school teachers and music instructors. Known for their expressive, elegant style of play and youth outreach.
club_values: Play in harmony, Pass with poetry, Sing with the fans

clubs.name: FC Zoryn Vatra
clubs.club_history: Zoryn Vatra was formed during wartime by resistance workers as a mobile sports club symbolizing the survival of culture through flame. 'Vatra' refers to the fire of resistance, and the club has retained that rebel identity — emphasizing community, courage, and youth upliftment.

clubs.name: Vernek Albion
clubs.club_history:
Vernek Albion was born during the interwar period, in a foggy hillside town known for craft guilds, windmills, and philosophical schools. Its football culture emerged from trade union roots and was later rejuvenated by eco-socialist thinkers in the 90s.
Today, the club is governed by a hybrid ownership model:
- 51% controlled by the Albion Cooperative (fans and locals)
- 49% funded by Albion & Partners, a progressive venture capital group focused on green infrastructure and social entrepreneurship.
Their home ground, Fogmoor Grounds, is entirely solar-powered, fan-designed, and famous for its tree-lined stands and misty morning warmups. It’s a spiritual football experience.
Albion isn’t about trophies (yet). It’s about doing football right — and maybe surprising a giant along the way.
clubs.club_slogan: “In Mist We March, Through Fog We Fight – Albion Burns the Brightest Light!”

clubs.name: Sunhollow FC
clubs.club_history: Established by solar energy pioneers and local gardeners, Sunhollow FC emphasizes eco-consciousness and joyful football.
club_values: Shine together, Grow local, Never dim

clubs.name: Thunderspire Rovers
clubs.club_history: A club from the misty peaks above Stravna, known for their aggressive vertical play and intense matchdays under dark clouds.
club_values: Strike fast, Storm the line, Survive the elements

clubs.name: Redbraid Harriers
clubs.club_history: Founded by cross-country runners turned footballers. Known for endurance, flank speed, and blood-red mountain kits.
club_values: Endure more, Outpace all, Earn the climb

clubs.name: Stravna Wakes
clubs.club_history: Stravna Wakes emerged from boating unions and local river festivals, combining sport and culture on water’s edge. They play open, flowing football mirroring the Velmoran river system. A proud cultural club, their chants echo off canoes and bridges every derby day.
clubs.club_slogan: We ride the current, we roar.

clubs.name: Stravna Velkomir
clubs.club_history:
Stravna Velkomir is one of Velmora’s oldest football clubs, with deep cultural ties to southern Velmoran tradition, regional music, and folk sport. Its name reflects grandeur (Velkomir meaning “great peace”), and the club acts as a cultural torchbearer for the south.
Backed by Aurek Partners LLP, a foreign private equity firm, the current ownership model is pragmatic. Though this irks purists, the board has preserved much of the club's local charm.
Stravna’s academy is renowned for producing technically gifted playmakers and tenacious full-backs. The club’s playing style is often fluid, expressive, and emotionally driven — sometimes to their tactical detriment.
The stadium, The Velkomir SkyDome, is a scenic, slightly sunken ground with open air stands, southern chants echoing from the hills. Matchdays feel like festivals, and the Lake-River Classic vs Drosna is a nationwide cultural event.
This is a club of heart over hype — a place where football meets folklore.
clubs.club_slogan: “Sing it Loud from Hill to Shore – Stravna Lives Forevermore!”

central-velmora.name: Central Velmora
central-velmora.description: The political and economic heart of Velmora, home to the capital city and the nation's most prestigious institutions.

clubs.name: Valdren Atletika
clubs.club_history:
Valdren Atletika was born in the industrial heart of Velmora, backed by the powerful Valdren Ironworks. Initially a worker’s recreation outlet, the club became a symbol of capital dominace in both sport and industry. Known for its rugged yet elegant playing style, Valdren rose to prominence between the 1930s and 60s, capturing multiple national titles.
In the 2000s, the club embraced modernization, balancing tradition with cutting-edge analytics and aggressive marketing. The fans — fiercely loyal — see the club as the soul of Velmoran football.
The Industrial Iron Derby vs Zarnov Union is the oldest in the country, with roots tracing back to factory strikes and urban class tensions. The club is also embroiled in rising rivalries with Braknov Spartak (military pride) and Velgrad '04 (media-fueled antagonism).
Today, Valdren Atletika is a national powerhouse, balancing history, ambition, and pressure like few others.
clubs.club_slogan: “From the Furnace to the Final - Valdren Never Bends!”

supporter_quotes.text: Every matchday is a pilgrimage. This club runs in my blood.
supporter_quotes.author: Mira D., North Stand

supporter_quotes.text: We don't support, we embody the roar.
supporter_quotes.author: Hadi R., Ultras Core

supporter_quotes.text: Win or lose, it's our anthem that echoes the loudest.
supporter_quotes.author: Lior G., South Curve

supporter_quotes.text: From the streets of Valdren to the heart of the Forge — we never miss a beat.
supporter_quotes.author: Kaela V., City Chant Crew

clubs.name: Red Hearth Wanderers
clubs.club_history: Founded by railway furnace stokers in the Zarnov Iron Belt, Red Hearth Wanderers is a gritty, old-school club with roots in transient labour unions and steam-era rail culture. The club got its name from the ironworks’ glowing furnaces — 'red hearts of the people.' Known for their nomadic early years, they’ve always played with fire in their bellies and mud on their boots. Overshadowed by Zarnov Union, they remain fiercely proud of their underdog identity and loyal support.

clubs.name: Zarnov Union
clubs.club_history:
Zarnov Union was born from the riveter syndicates and dockworkers' cooperatives in the industrial rise of Velmora’s eastern heartland. It’s the only major fan-owned club in the Velmoran top flight, governed by the Zarnov United Trust through a democratic model.
Their rivalry with Valdren Atletika is as old as the league itself, symbolizing everything from class warfare to regional pride. Fans call it The Iron Derby, but to locals, it’s just war.
Zarnov has long punched above its fi[]cial weight, producing legends from its academy and instilling fierce tactical discipline. The stadium, The Forge, is considered one of the most intimidating away days in Velmora.
The club’s 2025 title win broke a 56-year drought and was widely considered one of the greatest footballing moments in national history.
club_values: Power to the people, pride in the press.
clubs.club_slogan: Hammers High! Riveters Rise! Zarnov Fights with Iron Pride!

western-plateau.name: Western Plateau
western-plateau.description: A vast region combining historic cities and emerging footballing outposts.

clubs.name: Dockland Dandies
clubs.club_history: A rebellion against drab port football, the Dockland Dandies were founded by fashion-forward dockhands who mixed Saturday shipping shifts with Sunday style shows. Known for their flashy kits, ball flair, and anti-traditional stance, they’re Velmora’s footballing iconoclasts.

clubs.name: Velmorsk City
clubs.club_history: A commercial club spun out of the Velmorsk marina development project, Velmorsk City is sleek, stylish, and commercially ambitious. Known for technical football and smart marketing, they are the rising star of the coast.

clubs.name: Velmorsk Mariners
clubs.club_history:
Velmorsk Mariners are the old salt of Velmoran football — a club born on shipyards, raised on dock grit, and forever shaped by the roaring southern seas. Originally formed by maritime workers and naval engineers, the club has always stood for survival, resilience, and community strength.
Owned by VelPort Maritime, the club follows a conservative fiscal policy, prioritizing stability, sponsor reputation, and discipline. Players must fit the system — no room for mavericks.
Tactically, Velmorsk play structured, low-block football, known for grinding out results and strong set-pieces. They're often accused of being “anti-football,” but fans call it “nautical pragmatism.”
clubs.club_slogan: “Anchor Down, Rise with Tide – Velmorsk Fights from the Waterside!”

clubs.name: Anchor FC
clubs.club_history: Anchor FC began as a naval engineering club in Velmorsk’s dry docks. Originally backed by shipwright unions, Anchor has a militaristic edge — strict formations, high conditioning, and no-nonsense coaching. Their derby vs Dockside Union is known as “The Maritime Clash” and is a fierce fight for dockland supremacy.

clubs.name: Silverboot Rangers
clubs.club_history: Silverboot Rangers take their name from an old dockyard superstition — that silver boots prevent injury. The club has embraced the myth, using metallic kit accents and hard-tackling football as its hallmark. A cult favorite, Silverboot is fast, aggressive, and proud of its lower-league reputation.

clubs.name: Velgrad Spartans
clubs.club_history: Founded by ex-servicemen and academy coaches, Velgrad Spartans represent a disciplined and resilient football culture. They pride themselves on high fitness standards, tactical unity, and a no-nonsense work ethic.

clubs.name: Foxes of Velgrad
clubs.club_history: Velgrad’s underdog club, the Foxes are clever, scrappy, and opportunistic. Founded by local youth players and scouts, they built their brand on spotting hidden gems and upsetting giants with tactical cunning.

clubs.name: Velgrad '04
clubs.club_history:
Velgrad '04 was founded as a media-backed breakaway project by VelTV Sports Group, originally to represent the capital in a modern, forward-thinking way. Often dubbed the “Velmoran PSG”, the club blends heavy investment, branding savvy, and sporting ambition.
Though it lacks the deep roots of Valdren or Radomir, Velgrad '04 has quickly gained relevance thanks to smart signings, vibrant kits, and global marketing. Its youth facilities are good, but underused — preference still goes to ready-made stars.
Their stadium, Lion’s Roar Arena, is an architectural marvel with LED lighting shows and rooftop terraces — a symbol of the club’s high-production image.
While traditional fans across Velmora mock them as “plastic,” the club continues to attract young, urban supporters, and its climb into the top 4 has made it a serious title challenger.
clubs.club_slogan: “Lions Roar, Lights Ignite – Velgrad Owns the Capital Night!”

clubs.name: Dockside Union
clubs.club_history: Dockside Union was formed by stevedores and port clerks along Velgrad’s industrial docklands. The club rose through factory leagues in the 1920s, playing on gravel near freight rails. Known for gritty defense and storm-hardened players, the club symbolizes blue-collar endurance. Its fiercest rivals are Woolstack United and Anchor FC.

clubs.name: Woolstack United
clubs.club_history: Woolstack was founded by textile workers in Velgrad’s wool guild. The club has a strange mix of grace and grit — passing triangles learned on loom floors, yet physically domi[]t in duels. Their scarves are iconic across Velmora, knitted by fan collectives. A proud old club that believes in craft over cash.

clubs.name: Oakshroud AFC
clubs.club_history: Oakshroud AFC takes its name from the ancient oak groves surrounding their original pitch. Formed by environmentalists and scouts, the club emphasizes sustainability and youth. Tactically, they play a zonal press with smart rotations — like forest roots weaving underground. Calm, ethical, and well-organized.

clubs.name: FK Kravnov
clubs.club_history: Formed by railway miners from the Kravnov gorge, the club is known for harsh conditions, rough tactics, and loyal ultras. It's old-school, no-frills football in one of Velmora's most rugged towns.
clubs.club_slogan: Fall in the pit, rise with pride.

clubs.name: Old Karnov Grit
clubs.club_history: Old Karnov Grit is the elder football statesman of Karnov, having once dominated pre-league regional football. Today, the club is nostalgic, dogged, and beloved by purists. Their style mirrors a long-distance runner: slow start, explosive finish.

clubs.name: Karnov Ironfields
clubs.club_history:
Karnov Ironfields is Velmora’s toughest club — forged during the rise of Karnov’s vast ore mining industries. Named after the iron-rich plateaus surrounding the city, the club was built by and for miners, ironworkers, and welders.
Funded by Karnov Ore & Energy, the club’s fi[]ces are cyclical — booming with global metal prices, struggling when demand dips. This has fostered a culture of resilience and improvisation, both on and off the pitch.
The club’s aesthetic is plain: maroon kits, soot-covered scarves, and muddy boots. Their stadium, The Smelter, is low-built, rust-colored, and renowned for having the coldest away dugout in the league. No-frills football, surrounded by smoke and shouting.
They don’t win many, but they never lose without a fight. They’ve become a favorite among neutral fans who love grit over glamour.
clubs.club_slogan: “Dig Deep, Bleed Red – Karnov Rises, Iron-Bred!”

clubs.name: Saltstone Rovers
clubs.club_history: Saltstone Rovers began as a club for stonecutters in the Karnov hills. The pitch was once a literal stone quarry, flattened for play. The club prides itself on physicality and resilience, with a style rooted in aerial duels and set-pieces. Still family-owned, Saltstone is a symbol of Karnov’s proud rural labor class.

clubs.name: Waveroot Wanderers
clubs.club_history: Waveroot Wanderers were founded by forest trailblazers and creek fishermen on the Karnov outskirts. Their game style is chaotic yet opportunistic, reflective of their fluid home pitch by the marshes. They’ve never played above the 3rd tier, but they're respected for their unpredictability and close community ties.

clubs.name: Redbraid Harriers
clubs.club_history: Redbraid Harriers were founded by postal workers and hill runners. The club’s logo — a falcon with red-tied wings — reflects their high-tempo, man-marking system. Their unique tradition includes a pre-game cross-country run by academy players. They are Karnov’s fastest, if not flashiest, football team.

clubs.name: Thuvak Paper Kings
clubs.club_history: The Paper Kings were founded by pulp mill workers and remain deeply tied to the printing press and literary scene of Thuvak. The club sponsors reading initiatives and believes in sharp minds on and off the pitch.

clubs.name: Thuvak Harriers
clubs.club_history:
Thuvak Harriers were born from the agricultural cooperatives of the east — a team built by farmers, for farmers. Initially competing with equipment bought from rural auctions, they’ve grown into a fiercely self-reliant club rooted in community strength, resourcefulness, and stormy football.
Still owned by the Thuvak Rural Union, their ethos remains non-corporate, non-commercial — no flashy sponsors, no mega deals, just muddy boots, bursting lungs, and wind in their sails.
clubs.club_slogan: “Winds Rise, We Ride – Thuvak Roars with Farmer Pride!”

clubs.name: Gullwing Albion
clubs.club_history: Gullwing Albion was founded by schoolteachers and birdwatchers in Thuvak’s high cliffs. Known for fluid passing and wide play, the club often models itself after seaborne birds — agile and observant. Their kits feature wingspan motifs, and matchdays include nature hymns. Cultured, calm, and expressive — they are the poetic side of regional football.

clubs.name: Harborlight Athletic
clubs.club_history: Harborlight was formed by lighthouse crews and coast guards during wartime blackout patrols. The club’s emblem — a shining light tower — is both literal and metaphorical. Known for smart, tactical football and counter-pressing, Harborlight is as sharp on the pitch as their coastline is jagged. They play with intensity and vision.
